MAGTANGGOL T. GUNIGUNDO I 2nd District, Valenzuela City Room 21 2, North Wing Batasan Complex, Diliman Quezon City Dear Congressman Gunigundo: DILG Legal Opinion No. 53 s. 2012 JUL 26 2012 cunn RECORDS R FLEA D SIENATUE: 2 DAT". 'IRE: This has reference to your letter dated 14 May 2012 requesting clarification on the following issues: Since Barangay Canumay is located in Metro Manila, can two (2) barangays be created out of it by means of Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1 ? 2. If the answer to the above question is in the affirmative, when will the corporate existence of the two (2) new barangays begin? Will it be on the first election of the barangay officials, or will it be upon the ratification of Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1? 3. The other question is, in the interim, that is prior to the first election of the barangay officials of the two (2) new barangays, can the mayor appoint the said officials under the provisions of Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1 ? With regard to your first query, we reply in the affirmative. Sections 6 and 8 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 71 60) are instructive, thus: "SECTION 6. Authority to Create Locat Government Units.—A ZocaZ government unit maq be created, divided, merged, abolished, or its boundaries substantiaZZy altered either bv Zaw enacted bv Conqress in the case of a province, city, municipality, or any other political subdivision, ordinance pessed by the sangguniang panZaZawigan or sangguniang panZungsod concerned in the case of a barangay located within its territorial jurisdiction, subject to such limitations and requirements prescribed in this Code." "SECTION 8. Division and Merger.—Division and merger of existing ZocaZ government units shall comply. with the same requirement herein prescribed for their creation: Provided, however, That such division shaZZ not reduce the income, population, or tand area of the Zocat government unit or units concerned to less than the minimum requirements prescribed in this Code: Provided, further; That the income classification of the original ZocaZ government unit or units shaZZ not fau below its current income classification prior to such division. The income classification of ZocaZ government units shaZZ be updated within Six (6) months from the effectivity of this

Code to reflect the changes in their financial position resulting from the increased revenues as provided herein." (Emphasis Supplied) Clearly, based on the foregoing, a barangay within Metro Manila may be created or divided thru ANY of the following: 2. A law enacted by Congress; OR By ordinance passed by the sangguniang panlungsod. While the 2nd manner of creation or division as enumerated above is faster than the 1st manner, the 2nd manner appears however to be more disadvantageous to the local government unit (LGU) which through an ordinance officially created the particular barangay, since under Section 285 of the same Code, the financial requirements of the newly-created barangay/s shall be shouldered by the LGU which created it/them. Perhaps, in order to prevent this to happen or at least continue its implementation, House Bill No. 5890 was filed by Congressman Rex Gatchalian so that the two (2) newly-created barangays will be recognized in the entire country and that this time, the national government, not the City Government of Valenzuela will allocate the barangays' respective Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA). Per your representation, when a LGU is created by a law enacted by Congress, the national government, NOT the LGU which through an ordinance officially created the particular barangay, shall allocate an IRA. In the event that HB No. 5890 will be approved and become a law, we nevertheless find any problem with its implementation vis-å-vis Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1 by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Valenzuela City. It is settled that local legislative bodies exercise only delegated legislative powers conferred in them by Congressl. Such being the case, the law thereafter approved by Congress shall be considered to have superseded Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1 by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Valenzuela City. Pending the deliberation and approval of HB No. 5890 however, Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1 should be implemented. As to the second and third issues enumerated above, we are of the view that the corporate existence of the two (2) barangays should be reckoned from the appointment by the Mayor of Valenzuela City of the Punong Barangay, members of the Sangguniang Barangay, the Sangguniang Kabataan Cahirman and corresponding council in the Barangay where there are vacancies. Section 14 of the same Code provides: "SECTION 14. Beginning of Corporate Existence.—When a new Zocal government unit is created, its corporate existence shaZZ commence upon the election and qualification of its chief executive and a mqiority of the members Of its sanggunian, unless some other time is fixed therefor by the Zaw or ordinance creating it." The aforequoted provision of Section 14 of the Local Government Code provides for the general rule that the corporate existence of a local government unit, including barangays, shall commence upon the election and qualification of Magtajas vs. Pryce Properties and Philippine Amusements and Gaming Corporation, G.R. No, 111097, 20 July 1994.

its chief executive and a majority of the members of its sanggunian. Said provision, however, is immediately followed by an exception, i.e., "unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordinance creating it". Hence, if the law or ordinance creating a new local government unit is silent as to the time or period when its corporate existence shall commence, then the aforequoted Section 14 of the Local Government Code shall govern. On the other hand, if the law or ordinance creating a new local government unit provides some other time (other than that provided under Section 14 of the Local Government Code), then the corporate existence of the local government unit commences at such time. Section 5 of Ordinance No. 37, series of 2011 by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Valenzuela City provides and we quote: "SECTION 5. Appointment of Barangay Officiats.—The City Mayor, may appoint the Punong Barangay and members of the Sangguniang Barangay, and the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman, and corresponding council in the Barangay where there are vacancies. Such officials shaZZ hold office until their successors shalt have been elected in a regular elections for barangay officials following the approval and ratification of this ordinance." The conferment unto the City Mayor of the power to appoint the Punong Barangay, members of the Sangguniang Barangay, Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman and corresponding council in the barangay where there are vacancies should be taken as an EXCEPTION to the general rule found in Section 14 of the Local Government Code of 1991. Taking therefore, the legislative intent of Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1, we are of the view that the appointed Punong Barangay, members of the Sangguniang Barangay, Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman and corresponding council in the barangay where there are vacancies can already exercise those powers that are conferred by Ordinance No. 37, series of 201 1, the Local Government Code of 1991 and other existing laws and those that are implied therefrom at the time the corporate existence of the two (2) barangays commenced which, to our mind, has to be reckoned from the time of the appointment of the newly-appointed set of local officials therein. We hope we have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, ESUS B D UEIV Dir tor I Is/ 17 Copy furnished: RD RENATO L. BRION Norbertina Bldg., #2 East Ave. cor. EDSA Brgy.
